what_happened: The UK Parliament enacted the Explosive Substances Act 1883.
summary: On 10 April 1883, the UK Parliament enacted the Explosive Substances Act 1883. The Act makes it an offence to cause an explosion likely to endanger life or property, to attempt to cause one, or to make or keep explosives with intent or under suspicious circumstances. It is the earliest statute recorded in CTA6.

what_happened: The FBI's official history dates the founding of the federal investigative agency that became the FBI to 1908.
summary: The FBI's official history dates the founding of the federal investigative agency that became the FBI to 1908, in Washington, D.C. The exact date in 1908 is [UNKNOWN]. It is the starting point for the US federal agency that later led many terrorism investigations in CTA6 (for example T004 and T050).

what_happened: MI5 states that it has existed in different forms since 1909, beginning as the Secret Service Bureau.
summary: MI5, the UK Security Service, states that it has existed in different forms since 1909, beginning as the Secret Service Bureau. The exact date in 1909 is [UNKNOWN]. It is the earliest agency founding recorded in CTA6 for Europe.

what_happened: A bomb exploded on Wall Street; the FBI's history page states that those responsible were not identified.
summary: On 16 September 1920, a bomb exploded on Wall Street in New York. The FBI's history page calls it one of the Bureau's earliest terrorism cases; it says the best evidence points to a small group of Italian anarchists, but that those responsible were never identified and 'the mystery remains'.

what_happened: King Alexander I of Yugoslavia was assassinated; the Library of Congress record states that France then proposed a League of Nations convention on terrorism.
summary: On 9 October 1934, King Alexander I of Yugoslavia was assassinated in Marseille. The Library of Congress record for the 1937 League of Nations convention states that France then proposed a League of Nations convention on terrorism. The milestone links the assassination to the 1937 convention (T006).

what_happened: The League of Nations adopted the Convention for the Prevention and Punishment of Terrorism; the Library of Congress record states it never came into effect.
summary: On 16 November 1937, the League of Nations adopted the Convention for the Prevention and Punishment of Terrorism in Geneva. The Library of Congress record states it never came into effect. It is an early multilateral attempt to define and punish terrorism, and its definition is compared with a 2004 UN definition in milestone T079.

what_happened: The Oireachtas enacted the Offences against the State Act, 1939.
summary: On 14 June 1939, the Oireachtas (Irish parliament) enacted the Offences against the State Act, 1939. Its long title says it addresses conduct calculated to undermine public order and the authority of the State, regulates associations, and establishes Special Criminal Courts under the Constitution.

what_happened: The Convention on Offences and Certain Other Acts Committed on Board Aircraft was concluded.
summary: On 14 September 1963, the Convention on Offences and Certain Other Acts Committed on Board Aircraft was concluded in Tokyo. It covers acts affecting in-flight safety, lets the aircraft commander restrain a suspected offender, and requires States to take custody of offenders, according to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism. The UN lists it as the first of the international legal instruments against terrorism.

what_happened: The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft was concluded.
summary: On 16 December 1970, the Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft was concluded in The Hague. It makes seizing control of an aircraft in flight by force or threat an offence, requires severe penalties, and obliges States holding an offender to extradite or prosecute, according to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism.

what_happened: The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Civil Aviation was concluded.
summary: On 23 September 1971, the Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Civil Aviation was concluded in Montreal. It makes violence that endangers an aircraft in flight, and placing explosive devices on aircraft, offences that States must punish or extradite for, according to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism. A 1988 protocol later extended it to airports (T023).

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The UN General Assembly adopted resolution 3034 (XXVII) on measures to prevent international terrorism.
summary: On 18 December 1972, the UN General Assembly adopted resolution 3034 (XXVII) on measures to prevent international terrorism. The resolution set up a 35-member Ad Hoc Committee on International Terrorism. It is the earliest General Assembly action on terrorism recorded in CTA6.

what_happened: The UK Parliament enacted the Northern Ireland (Emergency Provisions) Act 1973.
summary: On 25 July 1973, the UK Parliament enacted the Northern Ireland (Emergency Provisions) Act 1973. It covers the trial and punishment of certain offences and offences against public security and order in Northern Ireland. It is one of the emergency laws later examined by the European Court of Human Rights (for example T016 and T025).

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of Crimes against Internationally Protected Persons was adopted.
summary: On 14 December 1973, the UN General Assembly adopted the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of Crimes against Internationally Protected Persons, including Diplomatic Agents. It requires States to criminalize murder, kidnapping and other attacks on heads of State, foreign ministers and officials entitled to special protection abroad, according to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism. The UN Treaty Collection holds it as a deposited treaty.

what_happened: The UK Parliament enacted the Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act 1974.
summary: On 29 November 1974, the UK Parliament enacted the Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act 1974. It provided for proscribed organisations, exclusion orders, and powers of detention and prosecution, as a temporary measure. It was followed by the 1989 Act (T027) and, eventually, the Terrorism Act 2000 (T049).

what_happened: The Council of Europe's European Convention on the Suppression of Terrorism (ETS No. 090) was opened for signature.
notes: An explanatory report has been identified but not yet read. The official treaty text supports the date and place; the words 'opened for signature' have not been confirmed from a fetched page, so this row stays not-proven.
summary: This milestone is not proven. The Council of Europe's European Convention on the Suppression of Terrorism (ETS No. 090) is recorded as opened for signature on 27 January 1977 in Strasbourg. The official treaty text, now the cited copy, supports the date and place ('Done at Strasbourg, this 27th day of January 1977'); an explanatory report that uses the words 'opened for signature' has been identified but not yet read.

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in Ireland v. the United Kingdom.
summary: On 18 January 1978, the European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in Ireland v. the United Kingdom, an inter-State case. According to the Court's factsheet, it concerned UK internment and five interrogation techniques used in Northern Ireland from 1971 to 1975, and the Court found a violation of Article 3 (inhuman and degrading treatment).

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in K. and Others v. Germany (no. 5029/71) on secret surveillance legislation.
summary: On 6 September 1978, the European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in K. and Others v. Germany (no. 5029/71) on secret surveillance legislation. According to the Court's factsheet, the Court found no violation of Article 8, accepting that, under exceptional conditions, secret surveillance powers could be necessary because of the threat of espionage and terrorism.

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The International Convention against the Taking of Hostages was adopted.
summary: On 17 December 1979, the UN General Assembly adopted the International Convention against the Taking of Hostages. It defines hostage-taking as seizing or detaining a person and threatening them to compel a State, organization or other third party to act or refrain from acting, according to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism.

place: Vienna, Austria and New York, United States
what_happened: The Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material was opened for signature.
summary: On 3 March 1980, the Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material was opened for signature in Vienna and New York. It criminalizes the unlawful possession, use, transfer or theft of nuclear material and threats to use it, according to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, and was amended in 2005 to cover nuclear facilities and domestic use, storage and transport.

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The UN General Assembly adopted resolution 40/61 on measures to prevent international terrorism.
summary: On 9 December 1985, the UN General Assembly adopted resolution 40/61 on measures to prevent international terrorism. It calls on all States not to organize, instigate, assist or participate in terrorist acts in other States, or to allow such activities on their territory, and to implement the Ad Hoc Committee's recommendations.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 579 (1985) on hostage-taking and abduction.
summary: On 18 December 1985, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 579 on hostage-taking and abduction, condemning unequivocally all such acts. It is among the Council's earliest resolutions on terrorism-related acts recorded in CTA6.

what_happened: France enacted Loi n° 86-1020 relative à la lutte contre le terrorisme.
summary: On 9 September 1986, France enacted Loi n° 86-1020 on the fight against terrorism. Days earlier, on 3 September 1986, the Constitutional Council had declared one article of the law unconstitutional and upheld the rest (T139). The law's specific provisions are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: The Protocol for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts of Violence at Airports Serving International Civil Aviation was concluded.
summary: On 24 February 1988, the Protocol for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts of Violence at Airports Serving International Civil Aviation was concluded in Montreal. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it extends the 1971 Montreal Convention (T010) to terrorist acts at airports serving international civil aviation.

what_happened: The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Maritime Navigation was concluded.
summary: On 10 March 1988, the Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Maritime Navigation was concluded in Rome. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it applies to shipping a legal regime similar to the aviation conventions, making it an offence to seize a ship by force or endanger its safe navigation.

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in B. and Others v. the United Kingdom (nos. 11209/84 and others) concerning detention under prevention-of-terrorism legislation.
summary: On 29 November 1988, the European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in B. and Others v. the United Kingdom (nos. 11209/84 and others), on detention under prevention-of-terrorism legislation in Northern Ireland. According to the Court's factsheet, it found a violation of Article 5 § 3 because holding suspects for four days and six hours or more before bringing them before a judge was not 'prompt'.

what_happened: Pan Am Flight 103 was destroyed by a bomb over Lockerbie, according to the FBI's history page.
summary: On 21 December 1988, Pan Am Flight 103 was destroyed by a bomb over Lockerbie, Scotland, according to the FBI's history page. The FBI says all 259 people on board and 11 people on the ground were killed, and describes it as one of the world's most lethal acts of air terrorism before 9/11. The UN Security Council later addressed it in resolution 731 (1992).

what_happened: The UK Parliament enacted the Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act 1989.
summary: On 15 March 1989, the UK Parliament enacted the Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act 1989. It covered proscription, exclusion, financial assistance for terrorism, and powers of arrest, stop and search and detention. It continued the temporary-provisions model of the 1974 Act (T014) until the Terrorism Act 2000 (T049).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 635 (1989) on marking plastic or sheet explosives for detection.
summary: On 14 June 1989, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 635 on marking plastic or sheet explosives so they can be detected. The Council condemned unlawful interference with civil aviation and called on States to cooperate in preventing terrorism involving explosives. A convention on marking plastic explosives followed in 1991 (T030).

what_happened: The G7 established the Financial Action Task Force to address money laundering, according to the FATF's history page.
summary: In 1989 (exact date [UNKNOWN]), the G7 established the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) to address money laundering, according to the FATF's history page. The FATF later added terrorist financing to its work (T057). The place of the decision is not recorded [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: The Convention on the Marking of Plastic Explosives for the Purpose of Detection was concluded.
summary: On 1 March 1991, the Convention on the Marking of Plastic Explosives for the Purpose of Detection was concluded in Montreal. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, parties must prohibit the manufacture and movement of unmarked plastic explosives and destroy or mark existing stocks within set periods. It follows Security Council resolution 635 (T028).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 731 (1992) concerning Libya and the Pan Am 103 and UTA 772 investigations.
summary: On 21 January 1992, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 731 concerning Libya and the investigations into the destruction of Pan Am flight 103 and UTA flight 772. The Council condemned the destruction of the two aircraft and the loss of hundreds of lives. Sanctions followed in resolution 748 (T032).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 748 (1992) imposing measures on Libya.
summary: On 31 March 1992, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 748, imposing measures on Libya. It required Libya to comply with the requests made under resolution 731 (T031) and to commit to cease all forms of terrorist action and assistance to terrorist groups.

what_happened: A bomb exploded in the parking garage of the World Trade Center, according to the FBI's history page.
summary: On 26 February 1993, a bomb exploded in the parking garage beneath the World Trade Center in New York, according to the FBI's history page. The FBI says it left a crater several stories deep and killed six people.

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The UN General Assembly adopted resolution 49/60 containing the Declaration on Measures to Eliminate International Terrorism.
summary: On 9 December 1994, the UN General Assembly adopted resolution 49/60, containing the Declaration on Measures to Eliminate International Terrorism. In the Declaration, Member States reaffirm their unequivocal condemnation of all acts, methods and practices of terrorism as criminal and unjustifiable, wherever and by whomever committed.

what_happened: The Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building was bombed; the FBI's history page records 168 deaths.
summary: On 19 April 1995, the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City was destroyed by a truck bomb; the FBI's history page records 168 deaths. The FBI page names the convicted perpetrator, which CTA6 does not repeat here. Why the event matters beyond the deaths recorded is not stated in the cited source [UNKNOWN].

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in M. and Others v. the United Kingdom (no. 18984/91) concerning the 1988 Gibraltar shootings.
summary: On 27 September 1995, the European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in M. and Others v. the United Kingdom (no. 18984/91), concerning the 1988 Gibraltar shootings of three IRA members by soldiers. According to the Court's factsheet, it found a violation of Article 2 (right to life) because the operation could have been planned and controlled without the need to kill the suspects.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1044 (1996) concerning Sudan and the attempted assassination of President Mubarak in Addis Ababa.
summary: On 31 January 1996, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1044 concerning Sudan and the attempted assassination of Egypt's President Mubarak in Addis Ababa on 26 June 1995. The Council condemned the assassination attempt as a terrorist act.

what_happened: The US Congress enacted the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996.
summary: On 24 April 1996, the US Congress enacted the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996. Its long title says it is an Act to deter terrorism, provide justice for victims and provide for an effective death penalty.

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The UN General Assembly adopted resolution 51/210, which established an Ad Hoc Committee on international terrorism conventions.
summary: On 17 December 1996, the UN General Assembly adopted resolution 51/210, which established an Ad Hoc Committee on international terrorism conventions. The resolution also condemns terrorism as criminal and unjustifiable and reaffirms the 1994 Declaration (T034). The Terrorist Bombings Convention was adopted a year later (T040).

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The International Convention for the Suppression of Terrorist Bombings was adopted.
summary: On 15 December 1997, the UN General Assembly adopted the International Convention for the Suppression of Terrorist Bombings. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it creates universal jurisdiction over the intentional use of explosives or other lethal devices in or against public places with intent to kill, seriously injure or cause extensive destruction.

what_happened: The Belfast (Good Friday) Agreement was concluded.
summary: On 10 April 1998, the Belfast (Good Friday) Agreement was concluded in Belfast. The UK Government page says it covered identity and citizenship and made commitments on decommissioning, security, policing and prisoners. It is the political settlement for Northern Ireland, where several of the UK emergency laws in CTA6 had applied.

what_happened: The Arab Convention for the Suppression of Terrorism was concluded under the League of Arab States.
summary: On 22 April 1998, the Arab Convention for the Suppression of Terrorism was concluded in Cairo under the League of Arab States. It is the regional terrorism treaty for League members; its provisions are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1189 (1998) after the bombings in Nairobi and Dar-es-Salaam.
summary: On 13 August 1998, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1189 after the 7 August 1998 bombings in Nairobi and Dar-es-Salaam. The Council condemned the attacks, which it said claimed hundreds of lives, and called on States to support the investigations in Kenya, Tanzania and the United States.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1192 (1998) on a trial in the Netherlands relating to the Pan Am 103 bombing.
summary: On 27 August 1998, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1192 on a trial in the Netherlands relating to the Pan Am 103 bombing. It required Libya to ensure the two accused appeared in the Netherlands for trial and kept earlier sanctions in effect. It continues the sequence that began with resolution 731 (T031).

what_happened: The OAU Convention on the Prevention and Combating of Terrorism was adopted (date as given on the AU treaty page; see NOTES.md).
notes: Pass 2 records the adoption-date disagreement as T145 (people-disagree): the AU treaty page gives 1 July 1999; the UN Treaty Collection copy, the AU status list and OAU decision AHG/Dec.132 give 14 July 1999.
summary: The OAU Convention on the Prevention and Combating of Terrorism was adopted; this row uses the date given on the AU treaty page, 1 July 1999, and the place is not recorded [UNKNOWN]. Other sources give 14 July 1999 at Algiers, a disagreement recorded as the people-disagree milestone T145. The AU page gives entry into force as 6 December 2002.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1267 (1999), establishing a sanctions regime and committee concerning the Taliban.
summary: On 15 October 1999, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1267, establishing a sanctions regime and committee concerning the Taliban. States were required from 14 November 1999 to apply measures including flight bans on aircraft operated by or for the Taliban. The regime was later extended and renamed (T104, T116), and its listings were challenged in court (T097).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1269 (1999) on international terrorism.
summary: On 19 October 1999, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1269 on international terrorism. It calls on States to implement the anti-terrorism conventions, to consider joining those they have not, and to cooperate with each other.

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The International Convention for the Suppression of the Financing of Terrorism was adopted.
summary: On 9 December 1999, the UN General Assembly adopted the International Convention for the Suppression of the Financing of Terrorism. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it requires States to prevent direct or indirect financing of terrorists, hold financiers liable, and identify, freeze and seize funds. Security Council resolution 1373 later made similar obligations binding on all States (T055).

what_happened: The UK Parliament enacted the Terrorism Act 2000.
summary: On 20 July 2000, the UK Parliament enacted the Terrorism Act 2000. It covers proscribed organisations, terrorist property, terrorist investigations and terrorist offences across the UK. It followed the earlier Temporary Provisions Acts (T014, T027).

place: New York, Washington D.C. and Pennsylvania, United States
what_happened: Hijacked aircraft struck the World Trade Center and the Pentagon and crashed in Pennsylvania; the attacks are examined in the 9/11 Commission Report.
summary: On 11 September 2001, hijacked aircraft struck the World Trade Center and the Pentagon and crashed in Pennsylvania. The attacks are examined in the 9/11 Commission Report (T077), and the FBI calls its investigation its largest case ever. Later the same month, the UN Security Council adopted resolutions 1368 and 1373 (T051, T055) and NATO issued its Article 5 statement (T052).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1368 (2001) condemning the 11 September attacks.
summary: On 12 September 2001, the day after the 11 September attacks, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1368. The Council said it was determined to combat by all means threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts, and its preamble recognizes the inherent right of individual or collective self-defence under the Charter.

what_happened: The North Atlantic Council stated that, if the attack was directed from abroad, it would be regarded as an action covered by Article 5 of the Washington Treaty.
summary: On 12 September 2001, the North Atlantic Council stated that, if the attack on the United States was directed from abroad, it would be regarded as an action covered by Article 5 of the Washington Treaty (collective defence). NATO's own page says this is the first and only time Article 5 has been invoked.

what_happened: The Authorization for Use of Military Force (Pub. L. 107-40) was enacted.
summary: On 18 September 2001, the Authorization for Use of Military Force (Pub. L. 107-40) was enacted. It authorizes the President to use all necessary and appropriate force against those he determines planned, authorized, committed or aided the 11 September attacks, or harbored them. Its continued application was later examined by the Congressional Research Service (CRS-R43983, unconfirmed copy).

what_happened: Executive Order 13224 on blocking property of designated persons was issued.
summary: On 23 September 2001, Executive Order 13224 on blocking property of designated persons was issued. The order states its objectives include preventing terrorism and denying financing and financial services to terrorists and terrorist organizations.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1373 (2001), which established the Counter-Terrorism Committee.
summary: On 28 September 2001, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1373, which established the Counter-Terrorism Committee. It requires all States to prevent and suppress terrorist financing, criminalize providing funds for terrorist acts, and deny support to those involved. The Committee's executive arm, CTED, was created in 2004 (T073).

what_happened: The USA PATRIOT Act (Pub. L. 107-56) was enacted.
summary: On 26 October 2001, the USA PATRIOT Act (Pub. L. 107-56) was enacted. Its long title says it is meant to deter and punish terrorist acts and enhance law enforcement investigatory tools. Some of its powers were later reviewed by the Justice Department Inspector General (T094) and the Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board (T109), and the USA FREEDOM Act reformed them in 2015 (T115).

what_happened: The FATF issued Eight Special Recommendations on terrorist financing, according to its history page.
summary: In October 2001 (exact day [UNKNOWN]), the Financial Action Task Force issued Eight Special Recommendations on terrorist financing, according to its history page. This extended the FATF, created in 1989 to address money laundering (T029), to terrorist financing. The place is not recorded [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: The US President issued a Military Order on detention, treatment and trial of certain non-citizens.
summary: On 13 November 2001, the US President issued a Military Order on the detention, treatment and trial of certain non-citizens, which created military commissions. The Supreme Court later held that the commission convened under it to try one petitioner lacked power to proceed (people-disagree milestone T090).

what_happened: The UK Parliament enacted the Anti-terrorism, Crime and Security Act 2001, including detention powers in Part 4.
summary: On 14 December 2001, the UK Parliament enacted the Anti-terrorism, Crime and Security Act 2001. Part 4 allowed suspected international terrorists who were not UK nationals to be certified and detained. Those detention powers were later found incompatible with the European Convention on Human Rights by the House of Lords (T080) and the European Court of Human Rights (T099).

what_happened: Canada's Anti-terrorism Act (S.C. 2001, c. 41) was enacted; the exact assent date is not shown on the fetched page.
summary: In 2001, Canada's Anti-terrorism Act (S.C. 2001, c. 41) was enacted in Ottawa. CTA6 lists the Act's date as 18 December 2001, but the exact assent date is not shown on the fetched page [UNKNOWN]. Its provisions are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: The Inter-American Convention against Terrorism was adopted by the OAS.
summary: On 3 June 2002, the OAS adopted the Inter-American Convention against Terrorism. This milestone is not-proven: the OAS treaty page could not be verified (HTTP 503/500), so CTA6 cannot confirm the text or details.

what_happened: The Council of the EU adopted Framework Decision 2002/475/JHA on combating terrorism.
summary: On 13 June 2002, the Council of the European Union adopted Framework Decision 2002/475/JHA on combating terrorism. It set common EU rules on terrorist offences, including a definition of a 'terrorist group'. It was followed in 2017 by Directive (EU) 2017/541 (T118).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1438 (2002) condemning the bombings in Bali.
summary: On 14 October 2002, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1438 condemning the bomb attacks in Bali, Indonesia, of 12 October 2002. The Council regarded the attacks, like any act of international terrorism, as a threat to international peace and security.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1440 (2002) condemning the hostage-taking in Moscow.
summary: On 24 October 2002, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1440, condemning the hostage-taking in Moscow on 23 October 2002 as a threat to international peace and security. The European Court of Human Rights later ruled on the rescue operation (see the Russia/Central Asia milestones).

what_happened: The Homeland Security Act of 2002 was enacted, establishing the Department of Homeland Security.
summary: On 25 November 2002, the Homeland Security Act of 2002 was enacted, establishing the Department of Homeland Security. DHS says it was created by combining all or part of 22 federal departments and agencies.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1450 (2002) condemning attacks in Kenya.
summary: On 13 December 2002, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1450. The Council condemns in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks in Kenya at Kikambala and Mombasa, including the bomb attack at the Paradise hotel.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1465 (2003) condemning a bombing in Bogota.
summary: On 13 February 2003, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1465 condemning the bomb attack in Bogota, Colombia, of 7 February 2003. The Council regarded the attack, like any act of terrorism, as a threat to peace and security.

what_happened: The Terrorist Threat Integration Center opened, according to NCTC's history page.
summary: On 1 May 2003, the Terrorist Threat Integration Center (TTIC) opened, according to the National Counterterrorism Center's history page. In August 2004 it was incorporated into the new National Counterterrorism Center (T078).

what_happened: The DOJ Office of the Inspector General released its review of the treatment of immigration detainees held in connection with the September 11 investigation.
summary: On 2 June 2003, the US Justice Department's Office of the Inspector General released 'The September 11 Detainees', its review of the treatment of non-citizens held on immigration charges in connection with the September 11 investigation. The review also examined the Department's decision to limit public information about the arrests; its findings are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: Peru's Truth and Reconciliation Commission (CVR) issued its final report covering 1980-2000; the release date is not printed on the fetched page.
summary: Peru's Truth and Reconciliation Commission (CVR) issued its final report covering 1980-2000; CTA6 dates it 28 August 2003. This milestone is not-proven because the release date is not printed on the fetched page. The report's findings are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1516 (2003) condemning bombings in Istanbul.
summary: On 20 November 2003, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1516. The Council condemns in the strongest terms the bomb attacks in Istanbul, Turkey.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1530 (2004) condemning the Madrid train bombings; the resolution's text attributed them to ETA (see NOTES.md on this attribution).
notes: Second source on attribution: SR-ESP-2008 (A/HRC/10/3/Add.2) describes the 11 March 2004 bombings as 'carried out by members of an international terrorist cell', while UNSC1530 attributed them to ETA. Recorded as a people-disagree row in timeline-add.csv.
summary: On 11 March 2004, the day of the Madrid train bombings, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1530 condemning them; the resolution's text attributed the bombings to ETA. A 2008 UN Special Rapporteur report instead describes them as carried out by members of an international terrorist cell, which is recorded as the people-disagree milestone T150. This row records only what the resolution says.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1535 (2004), establishing the Counter-Terrorism Committee Executive Directorate.
summary: On 26 March 2004, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1535, establishing the Counter-Terrorism Committee Executive Directorate (CTED). The resolution revitalized the Counter-Terrorism Committee created by resolution 1373 (T055), with CTED headed by an Executive Director. Its mandate was later renewed, for example by resolution 2617 (T131).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1540 (2004) on non-state actors and weapons of mass destruction.
summary: On 28 April 2004, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1540 under Chapter VII of the Charter on non-State actors and weapons of mass destruction. It requires all States to refrain from supporting non-State actors seeking nuclear, chemical or biological weapons, and the 1540 Committee was set up to follow its implementation.

what_happened: The US Supreme Court decided R. v. Bush, 542 U.S. 466 (2004), on federal court jurisdiction over habeas petitions from Guantanamo detainees.
summary: On 28 June 2004, the US Supreme Court decided R. v. Bush, 542 U.S. 466, on whether federal courts had jurisdiction over habeas petitions from Guantanamo detainees. It is the first of the Guantanamo detention cases recorded in CTA6 (see also T090 and T096); according to the syllabus, the Court held that US courts have jurisdiction to consider challenges to the legality of the detention of foreign nationals captured abroad in connection with hostilities and held at Guantanamo Bay.

what_happened: The US Supreme Court decided H. v. Rumsfeld, 542 U.S. 507 (2004), on due process for a US citizen detained as an enemy combatant.
summary: On 28 June 2004, the US Supreme Court decided H. v. Rumsfeld, 542 U.S. 507, on due process for a US citizen detained as an enemy combatant. The plurality concluded that such a citizen must be given a meaningful opportunity to contest the factual basis for detention before a neutral decisionmaker, according to the syllabus.

what_happened: The National Commission on Terrorist Attacks Upon the United States released the 9/11 Commission Report.
summary: On 22 July 2004, the National Commission on Terrorist Attacks Upon the United States released the 9/11 Commission Report. The Commission was mandated to examine the 11 September attacks (T050) and recommend ways to guard against future attacks. The Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act followed in December 2004 (T081).

what_happened: Executive Order 13354 incorporated TTIC into the National Counterterrorism Center, according to NCTC's history page.
summary: In August 2004 (exact day [UNKNOWN]), Executive Order 13354 incorporated the Terrorist Threat Integration Center (T068) into the new National Counterterrorism Center, according to the NCTC's history page. The page, published by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, is undated [UNKNOWN] and was confirmed through a text extraction only.

what_happened: Definitions differ: Security Council resolution 1566 (2004) describes terrorist acts in its own wording, while the 1937 League of Nations convention used a different definition.
summary: This row records two different definitions. Security Council resolution 1566 (8 October 2004) describes terrorist acts as criminal acts, including against civilians, committed with intent to cause death or serious injury or to take hostages, to provoke terror, intimidate a population or compel a government or international organization (UNSC1566). The 1937 League of Nations convention instead required parties to criminalize listed acts, such as wilful acts causing death, grievous bodily harm or loss of liberty to heads of State and others, when they were 'acts of terrorism' within its Article 1, as read in the scanned copy (LON-1937, item record LON-1937-LOC). CTA6 does not choose between them.

what_happened: Positions differed on Part 4 detention powers: the UK government had enacted them in the 2001 Act, and the House of Lords in A v Secretary of State held the related provision incompatible with the European Convention on Human Rights.
summary: This row records two positions on the UK's Part 4 detention powers. The UK government had enacted powers in the Anti-terrorism, Crime and Security Act 2001 to detain non-national terrorism suspects (UK-ATCSA2001). On 16 December 2004, the House of Lords in A v Secretary of State for the Home Department declared the related provision (section 23) incompatible with the European Convention on Human Rights (UK-AvSSHD2004). The 2005 control-order Act followed (T082).

what_happened: The Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 was enacted.
summary: On 17 December 2004, the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 was enacted. Its long title says it reforms the US intelligence community and the Government's intelligence activities. It came five months after the 9/11 Commission Report (T077).

what_happened: The UK Parliament enacted the Prevention of Terrorism Act 2005 (control orders).
summary: On 11 March 2005, the UK Parliament enacted the Prevention of Terrorism Act 2005, which created control orders. It followed the House of Lords ruling on Part 4 detention (T080). Control orders were abolished and replaced by TPIMs in 2011 (T106).

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The International Convention for the Suppression of Acts of Nuclear Terrorism was adopted.
summary: On 13 April 2005, the UN General Assembly adopted the International Convention for the Suppression of Acts of Nuclear Terrorism. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it covers acts against targets including nuclear power plants and reactors, as well as threats and attempts, and requires offenders to be extradited or prosecuted.

place: Geneva, Switzerland (UN Commission on Human Rights)
what_happened: The UN Commission on Human Rights adopted resolution 2005/80, creating a Special Rapporteur on human rights while countering terrorism (source text not machine-verified).
summary: This milestone is not proven. The OHCHR page on the Special Rapporteur states that in April 2005 the Commission on Human Rights created the mandate through resolution 2005/80, and that part is backed. According to an unofficial copy of the resolution (SEC-CHR-2005-80-SCR), it was adopted without a vote on 21 April 2005 and paragraph 14 appointed the special rapporteur for three years. The official resolution text could not be retrieved from the UN document system, so its adoption and contents are not machine-verified; confidence stays not-proven.

what_happened: The Council of Europe Convention on the Prevention of Terrorism (CETS No. 196) was opened for signature.
notes: An explanatory report has been identified but not yet read. The official treaty text supports the date and place; the words 'opened for signature' have not been confirmed from a fetched page, so this row stays not-proven.
summary: This milestone is not proven. The Council of Europe Convention on the Prevention of Terrorism (CETS No. 196) is recorded as opened for signature on 16 May 2005 in Warsaw. The official treaty text, now the cited copy, supports the date and place ('Done at Warsaw, this 16th day of May 2005'); an explanatory report that uses the words 'opened for signature' has been identified but not yet read.

what_happened: Bombs exploded on London's transport system; the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1611 (2005) the same day.
summary: On 7 July 2005, bombs exploded on London's transport system, and the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1611 the same day, condemning the attacks without reservation. The UK Home Office published an official account in 2006, and the Intelligence and Security Committee later reviewed the intelligence (T100).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1624 (2005) on incitement to commit terrorist acts.
summary: On 14 September 2005, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1624 on incitement to commit terrorist acts. It calls on all States to prohibit incitement by law in line with international law, to strengthen border security, and to promote dialogue among civilizations.

what_happened: The EU Presidency and the EU Counter-Terrorism Co-ordinator forwarded the European Union Counter-Terrorism Strategy (Council document 14469/4/05 REV 4) to the Council for agreement, for onward transmission to the European Council; the date of formal adoption is not stated in this document [UNKNOWN].
summary: On 30 November 2005, the EU Presidency and the EU Counter-Terrorism Co-ordinator forwarded the European Union Counter-Terrorism Strategy (Council document 14469/4/05 REV 4) to the Council for agreement, for onward transmission to the European Council. The document backs the date, place and document number; the date of formal adoption is not stated in it [UNKNOWN]. It is the EU's overall counter-terrorism strategy.

what_happened: The UK Parliament enacted the Terrorism Act 2006.
summary: On 30 March 2006, the UK Parliament enacted the Terrorism Act 2006. It created offences including encouragement of terrorism, dissemination of terrorist publications, preparation of terrorist acts and terrorist training.

what_happened: Positions differed on military commissions: the 2001 Military Order created them, and the US Supreme Court in H. v. Rumsfeld, 548 U.S. 557 (2006), held that the military commission convened to try the petitioner lacked power to proceed.
summary: This row records two positions on military commissions. The President's Military Order of 13 November 2001 created them (US-MILORDER2001). On 29 June 2006, the US Supreme Court in H. v. Rumsfeld, 548 U.S. 557, held that the commission convened to try the petitioner lacked power to proceed because its structure and procedures violated the Uniform Code of Military Justice and the Geneva Conventions (USSC-2006-548-557). Congress passed the Military Commissions Act later that year (T092).

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The UN General Assembly adopted the United Nations Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy (A/RES/60/288).
summary: On 8 September 2006, the UN General Assembly adopted the United Nations Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy (A/RES/60/288), with a plan of action annexed. The UN Office of Counter-Terrorism describes it as adopted by consensus. In 2017 the Assembly created an office to help States implement it (T121).

what_happened: The Military Commissions Act of 2006 was enacted.
summary: On 17 October 2006, the Military Commissions Act of 2006 was enacted. It authorizes trial by military commission of alien unlawful enemy combatants for violations of the law of war, and it restricted habeas corpus, a point later decided by the Supreme Court (T096). It followed the 2006 Supreme Court ruling recorded at T090.

what_happened: ASEAN member states concluded the ASEAN Convention on Counter Terrorism.
summary: On 13 January 2007, in Cebu, ASEAN member states concluded the ASEAN Convention on Counter Terrorism. Article I says it provides the framework for regional cooperation to counter, prevent and suppress terrorism.

what_happened: The DOJ Office of the Inspector General issued its review of the FBI's use of National Security Letters, as directed by the 2005 PATRIOT Act reauthorization.
summary: In March 2007, the US Justice Department's Office of the Inspector General issued its review of the FBI's use of National Security Letters, as directed by the 2005 PATRIOT Act reauthorization. It is an internal oversight review of a post-2001 investigative power; its findings are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1757 (2007) concerning the Special Tribunal for Lebanon.
summary: On 30 May 2007, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1757 concerning the Special Tribunal for Lebanon. Acting under Chapter VII, the Council decided that the provisions establishing the Tribunal would enter into force. It followed the investigation commission created by resolution 1595 in 2005.

what_happened: Positions differed on habeas corpus for Guantanamo detainees: the Military Commissions Act of 2006 restricted it, and the US Supreme Court in B. v. Bush, 553 U.S. 723 (2008), held detainees have the constitutional privilege of habeas corpus.
summary: This row records two positions on habeas corpus for Guantanamo detainees. The Military Commissions Act of 2006 restricted it (US-MCA2006). On 12 June 2008, the US Supreme Court in B. v. Bush, 553 U.S. 723, held that the detainees have the constitutional privilege of habeas corpus and are not barred from it by their enemy-combatant designation or their presence at Guantanamo (USSC-2008-553-723).

what_happened: Positions differed on implementing UN sanctions listings: the Court of Justice in K. and Al Barakaat (Joined Cases C-402/05 P and C-415/05 P) annulled the EU regulation as it concerned the applicants, on fundamental-rights grounds, while the UN 1267 listing regime continued.
summary: This row records two positions on UN sanctions listings. On 3 September 2008, the EU Court of Justice in K. and Al Barakaat (Joined Cases C-402/05 P and C-415/05 P) annulled the EU regulation implementing the listings as it concerned the applicants, on fundamental-rights grounds (CJEU-2008-C402-05P). The UN 1267 listing regime itself continued (UNSC1267). The UN later created an Ombudsperson for delisting requests (T101).

what_happened: Executive Order 13491 on ensuring lawful interrogations was issued.
summary: On 22 January 2009, US Executive Order 13491, 'Ensuring Lawful Interrogations', was issued. The order says it aims to improve intelligence-gathering, promote the safe, lawful and humane treatment of people in US custody, and ensure compliance with US treaty obligations.

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The ECtHR Grand Chamber delivered judgment in A. and Others v. the United Kingdom on detention under the 2001 Act.
summary: On 19 February 2009, the Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in A. and Others v. the United Kingdom on detention under the 2001 Act. According to the Court's factsheet, it found violations of Article 5 § 1 for most applicants because indefinite detention of non-nationals discriminated unjustifiably between nationals and non-nationals, while finding no violation of Article 3. It follows the House of Lords ruling at T080.

what_happened: The Intelligence and Security Committee published 'Could 7/7 Have Been Prevented?', its review of intelligence on the 7 July 2005 attacks.
summary: In May 2009, the UK Parliament's Intelligence and Security Committee published 'Could 7/7 Have Been Prevented?', its review of intelligence on the 7 July 2005 attacks (T086). It is a parliamentary oversight review of the work of MI5, MI6 and GCHQ before the attacks; its conclusions are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1904 (2009), creating the Office of the Ombudsperson for the Al-Qaida sanctions list.
summary: On 17 December 2009, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1904, creating the Office of the Ombudsperson for the Al-Qaida sanctions list. The Ombudsperson handles requests from those seeking removal from the list. The listing process had also been challenged in court (T097).

what_happened: The US Supreme Court decided Holder v. Humanitarian Law Project on the material-support statute.
summary: On 21 June 2010, the US Supreme Court decided Holder v. Humanitarian Law Project. It held that the federal material-support statute is constitutional as applied to the kinds of support the plaintiffs wanted to give to designated foreign terrorist organizations.

what_happened: The UN Special Rapporteur on counter-terrorism and human rights issued report A/HRC/16/51 on ten areas of best practices.
summary: On 22 December 2010, the UN Special Rapporteur on counter-terrorism and human rights, Martin Scheinin, issued report A/HRC/16/51, 'Ten areas of best practices in countering terrorism'. The report says it was his sixth and last annual report to the Human Rights Council and its predecessor. It is an output of the mandate recorded at T084.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolutions 1988 (2011) and 1989 (2011), separating the Taliban and Al-Qaida sanctions regimes.
summary: On 17 June 2011, the UN Security Council adopted resolutions 1988 and 1989, separating the Taliban and Al-Qaida sanctions regimes that had been run together since resolution 1267 (T046). Each regime continued the asset-freeze, travel and arms measures from earlier resolutions.

what_happened: The White House issued the National Strategy for Counterterrorism.
summary: On 28 June 2011, the White House issued the National Strategy for Counterterrorism. The document says it sets out the overarching goals of US counterterrorism and the steps needed to achieve them.

what_happened: The UK Parliament enacted the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures Act 2011.
summary: On 14 December 2011, the UK Parliament enacted the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures Act 2011. It abolished control orders, created under the 2005 Act (T082), and replaced them with TPIMs subject to set conditions, a five-year limit and court scrutiny.

what_happened: Norway's 22 July Commission delivered its report (NOU 2012: 14) on the 22 July 2011 attacks in Oslo and on Utøya.
summary: On 13 August 2012, Norway's 22 July Commission delivered its report (NOU 2012: 14) on the 22 July 2011 attacks in Oslo and on Utøya. It is the official Norwegian inquiry into the attacks; its findings are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The ECtHR Grand Chamber delivered judgment in E. v. the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia (no. 39630/09).
summary: On 13 December 2012, the Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in E. v. the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia (no. 39630/09). According to the Court's factsheet, it found the State responsible for the applicant's torture and ill-treatment in Skopje and for handing him to CIA agents in a secret 'rendition', a violation of Article 3. It is the first of several rendition judgments in CTA6 (see T110, T168, T181).

what_happened: The Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board issued its report on the Section 215 telephone records program.
summary: On 23 January 2014, the US Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board issued its report on the Section 215 telephone records program and the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court. The Board describes it as its first comprehensive study of a government program, with analysis and recommendations. The USA FREEDOM Act of 2015 later reformed these authorities (T115).

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in A.N. v. Poland (no. 28761/11).
summary: On 24 July 2014, the European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in A.N. v. Poland (no. 28761/11). According to the Court's factsheet, the Court found that Poland had cooperated in CIA rendition, secret detention and interrogation operations on its territory. A companion judgment was delivered the same day (T168).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 2170 (2014) concerning ISIL and the Al-Nusrah Front.
summary: On 15 August 2014, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 2170 concerning ISIL and the Al-Nusrah Front. It condemns their attacks on civilians and their recruitment of foreign terrorist fighters, and reaffirms that States must cut off arms and support to them. The broader foreign-fighter resolution 2178 followed in September 2014 (T112).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 2178 (2014) on foreign terrorist fighters.
summary: On 24 September 2014, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 2178 on foreign terrorist fighters. It requires Member States, consistent with human rights, refugee and humanitarian law, to prevent and suppress the recruiting, organizing, transporting or equipping of foreign terrorist fighters. Resolution 2396 (T124) built on it in 2017.

what_happened: The Senate Select Committee on Intelligence released the executive summary of its study of the CIA detention and interrogation program, published together with additional and minority views.
notes: Second source: CIA-SSCI-2013 (CIA's June 2013 response, approved for release 8 Dec 2014) states the Agency 'disagrees with assertions' in the Study. Recorded as a people-disagree row in timeline-add.csv.
summary: On 9 December 2014, the US Senate Select Committee on Intelligence released the executive summary of its study of the CIA detention and interrogation program, together with additional and minority views. The CIA had disputed some of the study's assertions in a June 2013 response, recorded as the people-disagree milestone T166.

what_happened: The UK Parliament enacted the Counter-Terrorism and Security Act 2015.
summary: On 12 February 2015, the UK Parliament enacted the Counter-Terrorism and Security Act 2015. It covers temporary travel restrictions, changes to TPIMs, data retention, transport security, and a duty concerning the risk of people being drawn into terrorism.

what_happened: The USA FREEDOM Act of 2015 was enacted.
summary: On 2 June 2015, the USA FREEDOM Act of 2015 was enacted. Its long title says it reforms federal authorities to require business records and conduct surveillance for foreign intelligence, counterterrorism and criminal purposes. It followed the oversight board's 2014 report on the Section 215 program (T109).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 2253 (2015), renaming the regime the ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida sanctions list.
summary: On 17 December 2015, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 2253, renaming the Al-Qaida sanctions committee the '1267/1989/2253 ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions Committee'. It extended the listing criteria to those associated with ISIL, adapting the regime that began with resolution 1267 (T046).

what_happened: Brazil enacted Lei nº 13.260 (anti-terrorism law).
summary: On 16 March 2016, Brazil enacted Lei nº 13.260, its anti-terrorism law. CTA6 confirmed the law's heading on the Presidency's website; its provisions are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: Directive (EU) 2017/541 on combating terrorism was adopted.
summary: On 15 March 2017, Directive (EU) 2017/541 on combating terrorism was adopted by the European Parliament and the Council. The Directive says it sets minimum rules on defining terrorist offences and sanctions, because Union-wide harmonised rules were needed. It followed the 2002 Framework Decision (T062).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 2349 (2017) on the Lake Chad Basin region.
summary: On 31 March 2017, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 2349 on the Lake Chad Basin region. The Council condemned attacks and abuses by Boko Haram and ISIL in the region, including killings, abductions and sexual violence.

what_happened: The US Government Accountability Office published report GAO-17-300 on federal countering violent extremism efforts.
summary: On 6 April 2017, the US Government Accountability Office published report GAO-17-300 on federal countering-violent-extremism efforts. As its title states, it found that actions were needed to define a strategy and assess progress; detailed findings are not recorded in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The UN General Assembly adopted resolution 71/291, establishing the Office of Counter-Terrorism.
summary: On 15 June 2017, the UN General Assembly adopted resolution 71/291, establishing the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism. The resolution's purpose, as its title states, is to strengthen the UN system's capability to help Member States implement the Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy (T091).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 2359 (2017) welcoming the deployment of the G5 Sahel Joint Force.
summary: On 21 June 2017, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 2359 welcoming the deployment of the G5 Sahel Joint Force, with up to 5,000 military and police personnel, to restore peace and security in the Sahel. The G5 Sahel had been established by a 2014 convention (T217), and the Council later addressed support to the force in resolution 2391 (T180).

what_happened: France enacted Loi n° 2017-1510 renforçant la sécurité intérieure et la lutte contre le terrorisme.
summary: On 30 October 2017, France enacted Loi n° 2017-1510 strengthening internal security and the fight against terrorism. France's National Consultative Commission on Human Rights had issued an opinion on the bill in July 2017 (CNCDH-2017, unconfirmed copy). The law's specific provisions are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 2396 (2017) on returning and relocating foreign terrorist fighters.
summary: On 21 December 2017, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 2396 on returning and relocating foreign terrorist fighters. It requires Member States to use advance passenger information, develop the capability to collect and analyse passenger name record data, and develop watch lists of known and suspected terrorists. It builds on resolution 2178 (T112).

what_happened: Two mosques in Christchurch were attacked; a Royal Commission of Inquiry later reported on the attack (26 November 2020).
summary: On 15 March 2019, two mosques in Christchurch, New Zealand, were attacked. A Royal Commission of Inquiry was set up and reported on the attack on 26 November 2020, and the Christchurch Call says governments and platforms launched the Call two months after the attack. The milestone records both the attack and the two official responses that cite it.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 2462 (2019) on countering the financing of terrorism.
summary: On 28 March 2019, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 2462 on countering the financing of terrorism. It reaffirms the financing obligations of resolution 1373 (T055) and requires States to criminalize terrorist financing in a manner consistent with international humanitarian, human rights and refugee law.

what_happened: The DOJ Office of the Inspector General issued its review of four FISA applications.
summary: In December 2019 (originally issued 9 December), the US Justice Department's Office of the Inspector General issued its review of four FISA applications and other aspects of the FBI's Crossfire Hurricane investigation. The report says it found serious performance failures by the agents responsible for the applications; these are the Inspector General's findings.

what_happened: The United States and the Taliban signed the Agreement for Bringing Peace to Afghanistan.
summary: On 29 February 2020, in Doha, the United States and the Taliban signed the Agreement for Bringing Peace to Afghanistan. The text includes guarantees that Afghan soil will not be used against the security of the United States and its allies and a timeline for withdrawing all foreign forces.

what_happened: The Philippines enacted Republic Act No. 11479, the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020 (source page not machine-verified).
summary: On 3 July 2020, the Philippines enacted Republic Act No. 11479, the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020. This milestone is not-proven: the Official Gazette page could not be verified (HTTP 403). Petitions against the Act reached the Supreme Court (T186).

what_happened: The National Security Council issued the National Strategy for Countering Domestic Terrorism.
summary: In June 2021, the US National Security Council issued the National Strategy for Countering Domestic Terrorism. The strategy says it is narrowly focused on violence that violates the law and threatens public safety, while protecting free expression.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 2617 (2021), renewing the CTED mandate.
summary: On 30 December 2021, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 2617, renewing the mandate of the Counter-Terrorism Committee Executive Directorate (CTED). CTED was to continue as a special political mission until 31 December 2025, with an interim review by the end of 2023. CTED was first created in 2004 (T073).

what_happened: The UK Home Office published CONTEST 2023, the UK counter-terrorism strategy.
summary: On 18 July 2023, the UK Home Office published CONTEST 2023, the UK counter-terrorism strategy. The Home Office states that CONTEST aims to reduce the risk from terrorism to the UK, its citizens and interests overseas, so people can live freely and with confidence.

what_happened: An international anti-anarchist conference met in Rome in November and December 1898; the historian Richard Bach Jensen describes it as the first international gathering convened to combat terrorism.
notes: The second citation (HIST-ROME1898-JCH) is unverified; the claim does not rest on it.
summary: In November and December 1898, an international anti-anarchist conference met in Rome. The historian Richard Bach Jensen describes it as the first international gathering convened to combat terrorism and the only Europe-wide anti-anarchist congress ever held. It is the earliest international cooperation milestone in CTA6.

what_happened: A secret anti-anarchist protocol was signed by Russia, Germany, Austria-Hungary and other states; the 1918 published text is dated 1/14 March 1904 (Julian/Gregorian), and Jensen gives 14 March 1904.
summary: In March 1904, a secret anti-anarchist protocol, known as the St. Petersburg Protocol, was signed by Russia, Germany, Austria-Hungary and other states. The text published in 1918 is dated 1/14 March 1904 (Julian/Gregorian calendars), and Jensen gives 14 March 1904. It followed the 1898 Rome conference (T133); the place of signature is not recorded [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: Singapore's Internal Security Act 1960 was enacted (statute remains in force per Singapore Statutes Online).
summary: In 1960, Singapore's Internal Security Act was enacted; Singapore Statutes Online shows it still in force. Its long title covers internal security, preventive detention and the prevention of subversion. Detentions under it are reviewed by an advisory board (T193).

what_happened: India enacted the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (Act No. 37 of 1967), per the Hindi text of the Act.
notes: The second citation (IN-UAPA1967) is unverified; the claim does not rest on it.
summary: On 30 December 1967, India enacted the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (Act No. 37 of 1967), according to the Hindi text of the Act. Amnesty International describes the UAPA as India's counterterrorism law (AMN-IND-2023); its provisions are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: A chapter on terrorism (Article 139) was added to Mexico's Federal Penal Code (amendment published in the DOF on 29 July 1970, per the consolidated code).
summary: A chapter on terrorism (Article 139) was added to Mexico's Federal Penal Code by an amendment published in the Diario Oficial on 29 July 1970, according to the consolidated code. Article 139 has since been amended, most recently in 2024, and now sets prison terms of fifteen to forty years.

what_happened: Chile's Law 18.314 defining terrorist conduct and penalties was published (promulgated 16 May 1984).
summary: On 17 May 1984, Chile published Law 18.314, which defines terrorist conduct and sets its penalties (promulgated 16 May 1984). The UN Special Rapporteur and the Inter-American Court later examined its use against Mapuche activists (SR-CHL-2014, T167), and it was repealed in 2025 (T191).

what_happened: France's Constitutional Council issued decision 86-213 DC on the 1986 law on combating terrorism.
summary: On 3 September 1986, France's Constitutional Council issued decision 86-213 DC on the 1986 law on combating terrorism. It declared Article 4 of the law unconstitutional and found the other provisions not contrary to the Constitution. The law was enacted on 9 September 1986 (T022).

what_happened: SAARC member states concluded the Regional Convention on Suppression of Terrorism (in force 22 August 1988).
summary: On 4 November 1987, SAARC member states concluded the Regional Convention on Suppression of Terrorism in Kathmandu; it entered into force on 22 August 1988. Under Article I, listed offences are treated as terroristic and are not treated as political offences for extradition.

what_happened: Türkiye adopted the Anti-Terror Law (Terörle Mücadele Kanunu, Law No. 3713), published the same day in the Official Gazette.
summary: On 12 April 1991, Türkiye adopted the Anti-Terror Law (Terörle Mücadele Kanunu, Law No. 3713), published the same day in the Official Gazette. Its article 1 (as amended in 2003) defines terror by reference to the use of force, violence or intimidation for listed aims, including changing the constitutional characteristics of the Republic. Parts of the law were later reviewed by the Constitutional Court (T216).

what_happened: Peru issued Decree Law 25475 setting penalties and procedures for terrorism offences (date per search listing; text captured).
summary: On 6 May 1992 (date per the search listing), Peru issued Decree Law 25475, setting penalties and procedures for terrorism offences; the text is captured. In 2003 Peru's Constitutional Tribunal declared parts of it unconstitutional (T202).

what_happened: Algeria issued Legislative Decree 92-03 on combating subversion and terrorism (Official Journal No. 70, 1 October 1992).
summary: On 30 September 1992, Algeria issued Legislative Decree 92-03 on combating subversion and terrorism, published in the Official Journal No. 70 of 1 October 1992. Its provisions are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in A. v. Turkey (no. 21987/93), concerning detention and treatment in custody in south-east Turkey.
summary: On 18 December 1996, the European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in A. v. Turkey (no. 21987/93), concerning detention and treatment in custody in south-east Turkey. According to the Court's factsheet, the Court found that the treatment amounted to torture (Article 3) and also found violations of Articles 5 and 13.

what_happened: Sources differ on the adoption date of the OAU Convention on the Prevention and Combating of Terrorism: the phase 1 AU treaty page gives 1 July 1999, while the UN Treaty Collection copy, the AU status list and OAU decision AHG/Dec.132 (Assembly at Algiers, 12-14 July 1999) give 14 July 1999.
summary: This row records two adoption dates for the OAU Convention on the Prevention and Combating of Terrorism. The AU treaty page used in phase 1 gives 1 July 1999 (OAU-1999). The UN Treaty Collection copy (UN-OAU1999-COPY), the AU status list and OAU decision AHG/Dec.132 from the Assembly at Algiers (12-14 July 1999) give 14 July 1999. CTA6 records both.

what_happened: Japan enacted the Act on the Control of Organizations Which Have Committed Acts of Indiscriminate Mass Murder (Act No. 147 of 1999).
summary: On 7 December 1999, Japan enacted the Act on the Control of Organizations Which Have Committed Acts of Indiscriminate Mass Murder (Act No. 147 of 1999). According to the Public Security Intelligence Agency, it came into force on 27 December 1999 and gave the agency new duties to investigate and request control measures. It is the basis for the Aum Shinrikyo observation measure renewed in 2024 (T228).

what_happened: Uzbekistan adopted Law No. 167-II 'On combating terrorism'.
summary: On 15 December 2000, in Tashkent, Uzbekistan adopted Law No. 167-II 'On combating terrorism'. Its stated purpose is to regulate relations in the field of combating terrorism.

what_happened: The Shanghai Convention on Combating Terrorism, Separatism and Extremism was concluded; the text reads 'Done at Shanghai, on June 15, 2001' and China's treaty database gives the signing place as Shanghai.
summary: On 15 June 2001, the Shanghai Convention on Combating Terrorism, Separatism and Extremism was concluded; the text reads 'Done at Shanghai, on June 15, 2001', and China's treaty database gives the signing place as Shanghai. The database records its entry into force on 29 March 2003. It defines terrorism, separatism and extremism for cooperation among its parties.

what_happened: The AU High-Level Inter-Governmental Meeting (11-14 September 2002) adopted a Plan of Action on the Prevention and Combating of Terrorism in Africa.
notes: The second citation (AU-POA2002-PSD) is unverified; the claim does not rest on it.
summary: On 14 September 2002, the African Union's High-Level Inter-Governmental Meeting in Algiers (11-14 September 2002) adopted a Plan of Action on the Prevention and Combating of Terrorism in Africa. The plan's preamble says AU Member States have long sought to counter terrorism individually and collectively.

what_happened: Sources differ on who carried out the 11 March 2004 Madrid train bombings: Security Council resolution 1530, adopted the same day, attributed them to ETA, while the UN Special Rapporteur's 2008 Spain report describes them as carried out by members of an international terrorist cell.
summary: This row records two accounts of the 11 March 2004 Madrid train bombings. Security Council resolution 1530, adopted the same day, attributed them to ETA (UNSC1530). The UN Special Rapporteur's 2008 report on Spain describes them as carried out by members of an international terrorist cell (SR-ESP-2008). CTA6 records both and does not decide between them.

what_happened: The Protocol to the OAU Convention on the Prevention and Combating of Terrorism was adopted (date of adoption per the AU treaty page).
summary: The Protocol to the OAU Convention on the Prevention and Combating of Terrorism was adopted; the AU treaty page gives 1 July 2004, and the place is not recorded [UNKNOWN]. It supplements the 1999 Convention (T045, T145); its provisions are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in Ö. v. Turkey (no. 46221/99), concerning the applicant's arrest and trial.
summary: On 12 May 2005, the Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in Ö. v. Turkey (no. 46221/99), concerning the applicant's arrest and trial. According to the Court's factsheet, it found that his conditions of detention did not violate Article 3; its findings on the arrest and trial are not recorded in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: Germany's Federal Constitutional Court (Bundesverfassungsgericht) ruled on the Aviation Security Act (1 BvR 357/05).
summary: On 15 February 2006, Germany's Federal Constitutional Court ruled on the Aviation Security Act (1 BvR 357/05). The challenge concerned the armed forces' power to shoot down aircraft intended to be used as a weapon against human life, and the Court declared section 14(3) of the Act incompatible with the Basic Law and void.

what_happened: The UN Special Rapporteur on counter-terrorism and human rights began a visit to Turkey (16-23 February 2006).
summary: On 16 February 2006, the UN Special Rapporteur on counter-terrorism and human rights began a visit to Turkey (16-23 February 2006) at the Government's invitation. The report says the visit aimed to gather first-hand information on counter-terrorism measures and their effect on human rights, and to begin cooperation with the Government.

what_happened: Russia's Federal Law No. 35-FZ 'On countering terrorism' was signed, after adoption by the State Duma (26 February 2006) and approval by the Federation Council (1 March 2006).
summary: On 6 March 2006, Russia's Federal Law No. 35-FZ 'On countering terrorism' was signed, after adoption by the State Duma (26 February 2006) and approval by the Federation Council (1 March 2006). A presidential decree had set up the National Anti-Terrorism Committee shortly before (T208).

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in S. v. Italy (no. 37201/06), concerning deportation of a person convicted in absentia of terrorism-related offences abroad.
summary: On 28 February 2008, the Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in S. v. Italy (no. 37201/06), on deporting to Tunisia a person convicted there in absentia of terrorism-related offences. According to the Court's factsheet, the Court held that the danger of terrorism does not call into question the absolute nature of Article 3, and found that deportation would breach it.

what_happened: Mali adopted Law No. 08-025 on the repression of terrorism.
summary: On 23 July 2008, Mali adopted Law No. 08-025 on the repression of terrorism, published in the Journal officiel. Its provisions are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: The International Commission of Jurists published the report of its Eminent Jurists Panel on terrorism, counter-terrorism and human rights ('Assessing Damage, Urging Action').
summary: In 2009, the International Commission of Jurists published the report of its Eminent Jurists Panel on terrorism, counter-terrorism and human rights, 'Assessing Damage, Urging Action'. The panel describes the report as based on one of the most comprehensive surveys of the subject and argues that many States' responses to 11 September 2001 undermined the international legal framework. These are the panel's own conclusions.

what_happened: Bangladesh's Anti-Terrorism Act 2009 (Act No. 16 of 2009) bears this date on the official laws site.
summary: Bangladesh's Anti-Terrorism Act 2009 (Act No. 16 of 2009) bears the date 24 February 2009 on the official laws site. Its provisions are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in F. and Others v. Russia (nos. 18299/03 and 27311/03), concerning the 2002 Moscow theatre hostage crisis and rescue operation.
summary: On 20 December 2011, the European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in F. and Others v. Russia (nos. 18299/03 and 27311/03), concerning the 2002 Moscow theatre hostage crisis and rescue operation. According to the Court's factsheet, it found no violation in the decision to use force and gas, but found violations over the planning and implementation of the rescue and the ineffective investigation.

what_happened: Argentina's Congress passed Law 26.734 amending the Penal Code on terrorism financing (promulgated 27 December 2011).
summary: On 22 December 2011, Argentina's Congress passed Law 26.734 amending the Penal Code on terrorism financing; it was promulgated on 27 December 2011. The law doubles the penalty range for offences committed to terrorize the population or compel authorities to act.

what_happened: Malaysia's Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (Act 747) received Royal Assent.
summary: On 18 June 2012, Malaysia's Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (Act 747) received Royal Assent. It provides special measures for security offences. Malaysia's human rights commission, SUHAKAM, later reported it had been used for non-terrorism purposes (SUHAKAM's assessment).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 2056 (2012) on the situation in Mali.
summary: On 5 July 2012, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 2056 on the situation in Mali. Among other things, it condemned the physical assault on Mali's Interim President; its other provisions are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in N. v. Switzerland (no. 10593/08), concerning Swiss measures implementing UN sanctions listings.
summary: On 12 September 2012, the Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in N. v. Switzerland (no. 10593/08), on Swiss measures implementing UN sanctions listings. According to the Court's factsheet, it found violations of Articles 8 and 13, observing that Switzerland could not simply rely on the binding nature of Security Council resolutions. It relates to the UN sanctions regime (T046) and to T097.
