what_happened: ECOWAS heads of state signed Supplementary Act A/SA.3/02/13 adopting the ECOWAS Counter-Terrorism Strategy and Implementation Plan.
summary: On 28 February 2013, in Yamoussoukro, ECOWAS heads of state signed Supplementary Act A/SA.3/02/13 adopting the ECOWAS Counter-Terrorism Strategy and Implementation Plan. The plan sets out actions by pillar, starting with every Member State's unequivocal rejection of terrorism as a serious criminal offence.

what_happened: Positions differed on the SSCI study of the CIA detention and interrogation program: the CIA's June 2013 response states the Agency disagrees with some of the study's assertions, while the committee's study (released December 2014) maintained its conclusions.
summary: This row records two positions on the Senate Intelligence Committee's study of the CIA detention and interrogation program. The CIA's response of 27 June 2013 states that the Agency disagrees with some of the study's assertions, including on the intelligence the program produced (CIA-SSCI-2013). The committee's study, released in December 2014, maintained its conclusions (US-SSCI2014).

what_happened: The Inter-American Court of Human Rights issued its judgment in N.C. y otros vs. Chile (Serie C No. 279), concerning convictions under Chile's Law 18.314.
summary: On 29 May 2014, the Inter-American Court of Human Rights issued its judgment in N.C. y otros vs. Chile (Serie C No. 279), concerning convictions of Mapuche leaders, members and an activist under Chile's anti-terrorism Law 18.314. The Court's findings are not captured, so the outcome is [UNKNOWN] in CTA6.

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in H. v. Poland (no. 7511/13), concerning secret detention in Poland under the CIA programme.
summary: On 24 July 2014, the European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in H. v. Poland (no. 7511/13), concerning secret detention in Poland under the CIA programme. According to the Court's factsheet, it found that Poland had cooperated in CIA rendition, secret detention and interrogation operations on its territory. The companion case is T110.

summary: On 3 June 2015, Amnesty International published a report on the Nigerian military's operations against Boko Haram in north-east Nigeria. Amnesty says it is based on more than 412 interviews and documents extrajudicial executions; the characterisation of certain acts as war crimes is Amnesty's own.

what_happened: Tunisia promulgated Organic Law 2015-26 on combating terrorism and money laundering, adopted by the Assembly of the Representatives of the People on 25 July 2015.
summary: On 7 August 2015, Tunisia promulgated Organic Law 2015-26 on combating terrorism and money laundering, adopted by the Assembly of the Representatives of the People on 25 July 2015. Its provisions are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: Egypt published Presidential Decree-Law No. 94 of 2015 issuing the Counter-Terrorism Law (Official Gazette No. 33 bis).
summary: On 15 August 2015, Egypt published Presidential Decree-Law No. 94 of 2015 issuing the Counter-Terrorism Law (Official Gazette No. 33 bis). Human Rights Watch criticized the law and referred to it by a different number, which is recorded as the people-disagree milestone T173.

what_happened: Sources differ on the number of Egypt's 2015 counter-terrorism law: the Official Gazette (No. 33 bis, 15 Aug 2015) shows Presidential Decree-Law No. 94 of 2015, while Human Rights Watch (19 Aug 2015) calls it 'Law 95 of 2015 for Confronting Terrorism'.
summary: This row records two versions of the number of Egypt's 2015 counter-terrorism law. The Official Gazette (No. 33 bis, 15 August 2015) shows Presidential Decree-Law No. 94 of 2015 (EG-LAW94-2015). Human Rights Watch, writing on 19 August 2015, calls it 'Law 95 of 2015 for Confronting Terrorism' (HRW-EGY-2015). CTA6 records both without deciding between them.

what_happened: The NPC Standing Committee adopted the Counter-Terrorism Law of the People's Republic of China (in force 1 January 2016; amended 27 April 2018).
summary: On 27 December 2015, the NPC Standing Committee adopted the Counter-Terrorism Law of the People's Republic of China. It came into force on 1 January 2016 and was amended on 27 April 2018. It is China's national counter-terrorism statute.

what_happened: South Korea enacted the Act on Counter-Terrorism for the Protection of Citizens and Public Security (Act No. 14071; text version effective 4 June 2016).
summary: On 3 March 2016, South Korea enacted the Act on Counter-Terrorism for the Protection of Citizens and Public Security (Act No. 14071); the captured text version is effective from 4 June 2016. Its enforcement decree followed on 31 May 2016 (T219).

what_happened: Germany's Federal Constitutional Court ruled on the BKA Act surveillance powers for countering international terrorism (1 BvR 966/09).
summary: On 20 April 2016, Germany's Federal Constitutional Court ruled on the surveillance powers given to the Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) for countering international terrorism (1 BvR 966/09). It is a constitutional review of counter-terrorism surveillance powers; the outcome is not recorded in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: Human Rights Watch published a report documenting alleged enforced disappearances and deaths during counterterrorism operations in Nairobi and north-eastern Kenya (allegations are HRW's).
summary: On 20 July 2016, Human Rights Watch published a report documenting alleged enforced disappearances and deaths during counterterrorism operations against Al-Shabab in Nairobi and north-eastern Kenya. The allegations and characterisations are HRW's.

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in T. and Others v. Russia (no. 26562/07 and others), concerning the 2004 Beslan school siege.
summary: On 13 April 2017, the European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in T. and Others v. Russia (no. 26562/07 and others), concerning the 2004 Beslan school siege. According to the Court's factsheet, it found several violations of the right to life, including a failure to take preventive measures despite specific threat information and serious shortcomings in the planning and control of the security operation.

what_happened: The UN Special Rapporteur on counter-terrorism and human rights began a visit to Saudi Arabia (30 April-4 May 2017).
summary: On 30 April 2017, the UN Special Rapporteur on counter-terrorism and human rights began a visit to Saudi Arabia (30 April-4 May 2017). The report says the visit assessed Saudi counter-terrorism law, policy and practice against international human rights law.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 2391 (2017) on support to the G5 Sahel Joint Force.
summary: On 8 December 2017, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 2391 on support to the G5 Sahel Joint Force. It reaffirmed the UN integrated strategy for the Sahel and set reporting arrangements on the force, following resolution 2359 (T122).

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in A.N. v. Romania (no. 33234/12), concerning secret detention in Romania under the CIA programme.
summary: On 31 May 2018, the European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in A.N. v. Romania (no. 33234/12), concerning secret detention in Romania under the CIA programme. According to the Court's factsheet, it found violations of Article 3 (owing to Romania's complicity and failure to investigate) and of Articles 5, 8 and 13. It is one of several rendition judgments in CTA6 (T108, T110, T168).

what_happened: Indonesia enacted Law No. 5 of 2018 amending its terrorism law (promulgated and in force 22 June 2018).
summary: On 21 June 2018, Indonesia enacted Law No. 5 of 2018 amending its terrorism law (Law No. 15 of 2003). It was promulgated and came into force on 22 June 2018. Komnas HAM had submitted a human rights position paper on the draft (T223).

what_happened: The UN Special Rapporteur on counter-terrorism and human rights began a visit to Kazakhstan (10-17 May 2019).
summary: On 10 May 2019, the UN Special Rapporteur on counter-terrorism and human rights began a visit to Kazakhstan (10-17 May 2019). Her report raises concerns that people accused or convicted of terrorism are held under exceptional detention rules; these are her assessments.

what_happened: The Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in Selahattin Demirtaş v. Turkey (No. 2) (no. 14305/17), concerning the pre-trial detention of an opposition party leader and member of parliament on terrorism-related charges.
summary: On 22 December 2020, the Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment in Selahattin Demirtaş v. Turkey (No. 2) (no. 14305/17), concerning the pre-trial detention of an opposition party leader and member of parliament on terrorism-related charges. The outcome is not recorded in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: The UN Special Rapporteur on counter-terrorism and human rights began a visit to Uzbekistan (29 November-7 December 2021).
summary: On 29 November 2021, the UN Special Rapporteur on counter-terrorism and human rights began a visit to Uzbekistan (29 November-7 December 2021). Her report notes reforms under way but raises concerns that security provisions are used to discourage criticism; these are her assessments.

what_happened: The Supreme Court of the Philippines decided C. et al. v. Executive Secretary (G.R. No. 252578) on the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020 (decision text not captured; docket page verified).
summary: On 7 December 2021, the Supreme Court of the Philippines decided C. et al. v. Executive Secretary (G.R. No. 252578) on the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020. This milestone is not-proven: the docket of petitions is verified, but the decision text could not be captured, so the ruling's content is [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: Human Rights Watch published a report on Sri Lanka's Prevention of Terrorism Act and the January 2022 amendment bill (assessments are HRW's).
summary: On 7 February 2022, Human Rights Watch published 'In a Legal Black Hole', a report on Sri Lanka's Prevention of Terrorism Act and the January 2022 amendment bill. HRW argues the proposed amendments would leave the framework largely intact; these assessments are HRW's. The amendment act was certified in March 2022 (T226).

what_happened: Nigeria's Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022 was enacted (Official Gazette No. 91, 16 May 2022).
summary: On 12 May 2022, Nigeria's Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022 was enacted (Official Gazette No. 91, 16 May 2022). Its stated objective is a unified legal, regulatory and institutional framework against terrorism, terrorist financing and the financing of weapons of mass destruction.

what_happened: The UN Special Rapporteur on counter-terrorism and human rights began a visit to Maldives (15-24 May 2022).
summary: On 15 May 2022, the UN Special Rapporteur on counter-terrorism and human rights began a visit to the Maldives (15-24 May 2022). Her report identifies human rights challenges in the Maldives' counter-terrorism and 'extremism' frameworks; these are her assessments.

what_happened: South Africa's Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Amendment Act 23 of 2022 received assent.
summary: On 23 December 2022, South Africa's Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Amendment Act 23 of 2022 received assent. It amends the 2004 Act, including provisions on training for terrorist purposes and disclosure of information.

what_happened: Chile's Law 18.314 was repealed, per the National Congress Library record (last modification by Law 21.732).
summary: On 12 February 2025, Chile's Law 18.314 on terrorist conduct was repealed by Law 21.732, according to the National Congress Library record. The 1984 law (T138) had been at issue in an Inter-American Court case (T167).

what_happened: Australia's Independent National Security Legislation Monitor provided its report on the definition of a 'terrorist act' to the Attorney-General (tabling due by 20 November 2026, per the Monitor's site).
summary: On 20 October 2026, Australia's Independent National Security Legislation Monitor gave the Attorney-General its report on the definition of a 'terrorist act'. The Monitor's site says the report is due to be tabled in Parliament by 20 November 2026. The definition matters because it sets the scope of Australia's terrorism offences, which is what the review examines; the report's findings are [UNKNOWN] in CTA6.

what_happened: The Internal Security (Detained Persons Advisory Board) Rules (G.N. No. S 23/1964), made under section 11(3) of the Internal Security Act, bear the date 16 January 1964; they govern the advisory board that reviews ISA detentions.
summary: Singapore's Internal Security (Detained Persons Advisory Board) Rules (G.N. No. S 23/1964), made under section 11(3) of the Internal Security Act, bear the date 16 January 1964. They govern the advisory board that reviews ISA detentions, which CTA6's notes describe as the statutory review body in a country without a national human rights institution.

what_happened: Sri Lanka's Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act is numbered No. 48 of 1979 (number and year as given by the Ministry of Justice; day and month [UNKNOWN]).
summary: Sri Lanka's Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act is numbered No. 48 of 1979, as given by the Ministry of Justice; the day and month are [UNKNOWN]. The Act was amended in 2022 (T226) and has been criticized by Human Rights Watch (T187).

what_happened: Pakistan's Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (XXVII of 1997) was enacted; its section 1(3) states that it 'shall come in to force at once' (day and month not in the captured copies [UNKNOWN]).
summary: In 1997, Pakistan's Anti-Terrorism Act (XXVII of 1997) was enacted; its section 1(3) states that it 'shall come in to force at once'. The day and month are not in the captured copies [UNKNOWN]. Its provisions include when an organization is 'concerned in terrorism', for example by committing, preparing for, or promoting terrorism (PK-NACTA-ATA).

what_happened: The Inter-American Court of Human Rights delivered its merits judgment in L.T. v. Peru (Serie C No. 33), a case the Inter-American Commission submitted on 12 January 1995 alleging unlawful detention, torture and a second trial on the same facts.
summary: On 17 September 1997, the Inter-American Court of Human Rights delivered its merits judgment in L.T. v. Peru (Serie C No. 33). The Commission had submitted the case on 12 January 1995, alleging unlawful detention, torture and a second trial on the same facts. The Court's overall ruling is not in the captured text [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: The Inter-American Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment on merits, reparations and costs in C.P. et al. v. Peru (Serie C No. 52), concerning four Chilean nationals tried by a military tribunal with anonymous judges under Decree-Law No. 25.659, as described in the judgment.
summary: On 30 May 1999, the Inter-American Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment on merits, reparations and costs in C.P. et al. v. Peru (Serie C No. 52). As described in the judgment, the case concerns four Chilean nationals tried by a military tribunal with anonymous judges under Decree-Law No. 25.659. The Court's ruling is not in the captured text [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: The Inter-American Court of Human Rights delivered its merits judgment in C.B. v. Peru (Serie C No. 69).
summary: On 18 August 2000, the Inter-American Court of Human Rights delivered its merits judgment in C.B. v. Peru (Serie C No. 69). The Commission had found violations of liberty, personal integrity and judicial guarantees; the Court's own ruling is not in the captured text [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: Heads of state of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation adopted the Agreement on the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS).
summary: On 7 June 2002, in Saint Petersburg, heads of state of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation adopted the Agreement on the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS). The SCO's record shows it in force from signature; it is the basis of the RATS body.

what_happened: Japan promulgated Act No. 67 of 2002 on the punishment of the provision of funds for criminal acts intended to intimidate the public (terrorist financing).
summary: On 12 June 2002, Japan promulgated Act No. 67 of 2002, which punishes the provision of funds for criminal acts intended to intimidate the public (terrorist financing). According to the National Diet Library record, the Cabinet submitted the bill to the 154th Diet session, and the Act is classified as criminal law.

what_happened: Australia's Security Legislation Amendment (Terrorism) Act 2002 (No. 65, 2002) became law (assent date not in the captured page [UNKNOWN]).
summary: In 2002, Australia's Security Legislation Amendment (Terrorism) Act 2002 (No. 65, 2002) became law, as shown on the Federal Register of Legislation. As its title states, it amended Australian security legislation on terrorism. The exact assent date is not in the captured page [UNKNOWN]; a search listing gives 5 July 2002.

what_happened: Peru's Constitutional Tribunal (Exp. No. 010-2002-AI/TC) declared a challenge to the 1992 anti-terrorism decree-laws founded in part and declared unconstitutional, among other provisions, article 7 and subsection (h) of article 13 of Decree-Law No. 25475.
summary: On 3 January 2003, Peru's Constitutional Tribunal (Exp. No. 010-2002-AI/TC) declared a challenge to the 1992 anti-terrorism decree-laws founded in part. It declared unconstitutional, among other provisions, Article 7 and Article 13(h) of Decree-Law No. 25475 (T142).

what_happened: Turkmenistan's law 'On combating terrorism' was adopted, as stated in the 2013 amending law (Vedomosti Mejlisa 2003, No. 3, art. 28).
summary: On 15 August 2003, Turkmenistan's law 'On combating terrorism' was adopted, as stated in the 2013 amending law (Vedomosti Mejlisa 2003, No. 3, art. 28). The law itself was not captured; CTA6 relies on the 2013 amendment, which updated the names of the agencies listed in it.

what_happened: Argentina's Public Prosecutor's Office created the Prosecution Unit for the AMIA case (UFI-AMIA) by Resolución MP N°84/04 (day and month [UNKNOWN]).
summary: In 2004, Argentina's Public Prosecutor's Office created the Prosecution Unit for the AMIA case (UFI-AMIA) by Resolución MP N°84/04; the day and month are [UNKNOWN]. The unit works with the prosecutors investigating the 18 July 1994 attack on the AMIA building.

what_happened: An Australian Senate committee published its report 'Bali 2002: Security threats to Australians in South East Asia'.
summary: On 12 August 2004, an Australian Senate committee (Foreign Affairs, Defence and Trade) published 'Bali 2002: Security threats to Australians in South East Asia'. The report examined intelligence reports, threat assessments and travel advice before the Bali attacks of 12 October 2002, and it includes remarks by Government Senators and a dissenting report. Its findings are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: India's Prevention of Terrorism (Repeal) Act, 2004 (No. 26 of 2004) repealed the Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002, with effect deemed from 21 September 2004.
summary: On 21 December 2004, India's Prevention of Terrorism (Repeal) Act, 2004 (No. 26 of 2004) repealed the Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002, with effect deemed from 21 September 2004. It ended India's 2002 terrorism law.

what_happened: Argentina's Decree 812/2005 approved the record of a 4 March 2005 hearing before the Inter-American Commission (petition No. 12.204) in which the State recognised responsibility in connection with the 18 July 1994 attack on the AMIA building.
summary: On 12 July 2005, Argentina's Decree 812/2005 approved the record of a 4 March 2005 hearing before the Inter-American Commission (petition No. 12.204). what_happened: Presidential Decree No. 116 'On measures to counter terrorism' established Russia's National Anti-Terrorism Committee (point 1).
summary: On 15 February 2006, Russian Presidential Decree No. 116 'On measures to counter terrorism' established the National Anti-Terrorism Committee (point 1). Russia's federal law on countering terrorism followed on 6 March 2006 (T155).

what_happened: Algeria's President issued Ordinance No. 06-01 implementing the Charter for Peace and National Reconciliation; it was published in the Journal officiel No. 11 of 28 February 2006.
summary: On 27 February 2006, Algeria's President issued Ordinance No. 06-01 implementing the Charter for Peace and National Reconciliation, published in the Journal officiel No. 11 of 28 February 2006. Article 1 says it aims to implement the Charter and complete the policy of peace and national reconciliation. Parliament approved it in April 2006 (T210).

what_happened: Algeria's Law No. 06-07 approved Ordinance No. 06-01 after approval by Parliament.
summary: On 17 April 2006, Algeria's Law No. 06-07 approved Ordinance No. 06-01 after approval by Parliament. This gave parliamentary approval to the ordinance implementing the Charter for Peace and National Reconciliation (T209).

what_happened: Kyrgyzstan's Law No. 178 'On countering terrorism' bears the date 8 November 2006 (date and number from the official database's page title; text not read).
summary: Kyrgyzstan's Law No. 178 'On countering terrorism' bears the date 8 November 2006. The date and number come from the official database's page title; the text was not read, so its content is [UNKNOWN] in CTA6.

what_happened: Colombia enacted Ley 1121 de 2006 on the prevention, detection, investigation and punishment of the financing of terrorism; it was published in Diario Oficial No. 46.497 on 30 December 2006.
summary: On 29 December 2006, Colombia enacted Ley 1121 de 2006 on the prevention, detection, investigation and punishment of terrorism financing; it was published in Diario Oficial No. 46.497 on 30 December 2006. It sets obligations for supervised financial institutions.

what_happened: India's National Investigation Agency Act, 2008 (Act No. 34 of 2008) bears the date 31 December 2008 (Hindi text).
summary: India's National Investigation Agency Act, 2008 (Act No. 34 of 2008) bears the date 31 December 2008 in its Hindi text. It is the law that created India's National Investigation Agency.

what_happened: The Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation adopted the SCO Convention against Terrorism.
summary: On 16 June 2009, in Yekaterinburg, the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation adopted the SCO Convention against Terrorism. what_happened: Pakistan's National Counter Terrorism Authority Act, 2013 (Act No. XIX of 2013) established the National Counter Terrorism Authority (day and month [UNKNOWN]).
summary: In 2013, Pakistan's National Counter Terrorism Authority Act (Act No. XIX of 2013) established the National Counter Terrorism Authority; the day and month are [UNKNOWN]. The Act's preamble says a focal institution was needed to unify the national response to terrorism and extremism.

what_happened: Türkiye's Constitutional Court decided case E. 2012/100, K. 2013/84 on a petition by 123 members of parliament concerning Law No. 6352, including its amendments to article 10 of Anti-Terror Law No. 3713; the decision was published in the Resmî Gazete on 2 August 2013 (No. 28726).
summary: On 4 July 2013, Türkiye's Constitutional Court decided case E. 2012/100, K. 2013/84 on a petition by 123 members of parliament concerning Law No. 6352, including its amendments to article 10 of Anti-Terror Law No. 3713 (T141). The decision was published in the Resmî Gazete on 2 August 2013 (No. 28726); its outcome on each provision is not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: The conference of heads of state of the G5 Sahel adopted the Convention establishing the G5 Sahel; Mali ratified it by Decree No. 2015-128 (as listed by Mali's Secretariat General of Government).
summary: On 19 December 2014, the conference of heads of state of the G5 Sahel adopted the Convention establishing the G5 Sahel in Nouakchott; Mali ratified it by Decree No. 2015-128, as listed by Mali's Secretariat General of Government. The G5 Sahel later deployed a joint force welcomed by the UN Security Council (T122). The convention text, read by OCR in round 4, closes 'Fait à Nouakchott, le 19 décembre 2014' with signature blocks for the five heads of state.

what_happened: The Maldives Government Gazette (vol. 44, no. 288) published Law No. 32/2015 on terrorism (Dhivehi text).
summary: On 28 October 2015, the Maldives Government Gazette (vol. 44, no. 288) published Law No. 32/2015, the Prevention of Terrorism Act, in Dhivehi. The UN Special Rapporteur later found the Anti-Terrorism Act vaguely defined (T189).

what_happened: Korea enacted the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Anti-Terrorism for the Protection of Citizens and Public Security (Presidential Decree No. 27203), in force from 4 June 2016.
summary: On 31 May 2016, South Korea enacted the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Anti-Terrorism for the Protection of Citizens and Public Security (Presidential Decree No. 27203), in force from 4 June 2016. It implements the 2016 Act (T175).

what_happened: The Knesset passed the Counter-Terrorism Law, 5776-2016; it was published in Sefer HaHukim No. 2556 on 23 June 2016.
summary: On 15 June 2016, the Knesset passed the Counter-Terrorism Law, 5776-2016; it was published in Sefer HaHukim No. 2556 on 23 June 2016. As its title states, it is Israel's counter-terrorism statute; its provisions are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: The UN Special Rapporteur on human rights while countering terrorism visited Sri Lanka from 10 to 14 July 2017 to assess its counter-terrorism policies, laws and practices.
summary: From 10 to 14 July 2017, the UN Special Rapporteur on human rights while countering terrorism visited Sri Lanka to assess its counter-terrorism policies, laws and practices since the end of its internal armed conflict. The report links progress in these areas to accountability and reconciliation.

what_happened: Australia's Independent National Security Legislation Monitor completed statutory reviews of stop, search and seize powers, declared areas, control orders and preventative detention orders.
summary: On 7 September 2017, Australia's Independent National Security Legislation Monitor completed statutory reviews of stop, search and seize powers, declared areas, control orders and preventative detention orders. A public hearing was held on 19 May 2017, and a parliamentary committee published its own reports on the same powers on 1 March 2018. The reviews were required by statutory deadlines, which shows these powers were subject to periodic independent review.

what_happened: Indonesia's National Human Rights Commission (Komnas HAM) submitted a position paper on the draft amendment to the anti-terrorism law to the chair of the parliamentary working committee on the bill.
summary: On 16 April 2018, Indonesia's National Human Rights Commission (Komnas HAM) submitted a position paper on the draft amendment to the anti-terrorism law to the chair of the parliamentary working committee on the bill. Among other points, it recommended a criminal justice approach that puts legal process and human rights first. The amendment was enacted as Law No. 5 of 2018 (T182).

place: [UNKNOWN] (African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights)
what_happened: The African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights delivered its merits judgment in A. v. Republic of Benin (Application No. 013/2017), which concerned proceedings including those before Benin's Court for the Repression of Economic Offences and Terrorism (CRIET).
summary: On 29 March 2019, the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights delivered its merits judgment in A. v. Republic of Benin (Application No. 013/2017), which concerned proceedings including those before Benin's Court for the Repression of Economic Offences and Terrorism (CRIET). The outcome is not recorded in CTA6 [UNKNOWN]; the place is also [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: The Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka published the executive summary of its 2018 prison study, which includes a section on prisoners held under the Prevention of Terrorism Act.
summary: On 25 November 2020, in Colombo, the Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka published the executive summary of its 2018 prison study, which includes a section on prisoners held under the Prevention of Terrorism Act. Its findings are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: Sri Lanka's Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) (Amendment) Act, No. 12 of 2022 was certified; it was published as a Gazette supplement on 1 April 2022.
summary: On 29 March 2022, Sri Lanka's Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) (Amendment) Act, No. 12 of 2022 was certified, and it was published as a Gazette supplement on 1 April 2022. It amends the 1979 Act (T194); Human Rights Watch had argued the bill left the framework largely intact (T187).

what_happened: Nigeria's National Human Rights Commission announced and inaugurated the Special Independent Investigative Panel on human rights violations in counter-insurgency operations in the North East (SIIP North-East).
summary: On 7 February 2023, Nigeria's National Human Rights Commission announced and inaugurated the Special Independent Investigative Panel on human rights violations in counter-insurgency operations in the North East (SIIP North-East). The Commission's summary says the panel was set up to investigate allegations in Reuters reports of December 2022 against the Nigerian military. Its report was posted in November 2024 (T229).

what_happened: Japan's Public Security Examination Commission decided, on the request of the Public Security Intelligence Agency, to renew the observation measure on the organisation known as Aum Shinrikyo (the agency describes it as the eighth renewal).
summary: On 12 January 2024, Japan's Public Security Examination Commission, at the request of the Public Security Intelligence Agency, decided to renew the observation measure on the organisation known as Aum Shinrikyo; the agency describes it as the eighth renewal. The measure rests on the 1999 Act on organizations that committed indiscriminate mass murder (T146).

what_happened: Nigeria's National Human Rights Commission posted the report of the SIIP North-East panel.
summary: On 9 November 2024, Nigeria's National Human Rights Commission posted the report of the SIIP North-East panel on human rights violations in counter-insurgency operations. It concludes the inquiry begun in February 2023 (T227); its findings are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: Papua New Guinea's Parliament passed the Counter-Terrorism Bill 2024 by 84 votes to 0, according to the Department of Prime Minister and National Executive Council.
summary: On 28 November 2024, Papua New Guinea's Parliament passed the Counter-Terrorism Bill 2024 by 84 votes to 0, according to the Department of Prime Minister and National Executive Council. The department's release says the vote exceeded the 60-vote absolute majority needed and that the Prime Minister called it a 'monumental, milestone law' (his description). The text of the Act itself could not be retrieved [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: The National Human Rights Commission of Korea submitted its opinion to the National Assembly in connection with deliberation of the draft Terrorism Prevention Act.
summary: On 30 November 2001 the National Human Rights Commission of Korea submitted an opinion to the National Assembly on the draft Terrorism Prevention Act then under deliberation, according to its press release of 1 December 2001. The content of the opinion is not recorded in CTA6 [UNKNOWN]. It is the first of three Korean oversight records in CTA6, with T232 and T236.

what_happened: The National Human Rights Commission of Korea announced that its chairperson would deliver the Commission's opposing opinion on the pending draft Terrorism Prevention Act to the Speaker of the National Assembly that afternoon.
summary: On 4 April 2002 the National Human Rights Commission of Korea posted a notice that its chairperson would visit the National Assembly that afternoon to deliver the Commission's opposing opinion on the pending draft Terrorism Prevention Act. The notice attaches a summary of the opinion, which CTA6 has not read [UNKNOWN]. It follows the Commission's November 2001 submission (T231).

what_happened: Mexico's Diario Oficial de la Federación published a decree, promulgated on 12 March 2014, that reformed article 139 (terrorism) of the Federal Penal Code and added a chapter on the financing of terrorism (articles 139 Quáter and 139 Quinquies).
summary: On 14 March 2014 the Diario Oficial de la Federación published a decree amending Mexico's Federal Penal Code and four other federal laws; the President signed it for publication on 12 March 2014. The decree rewrote article 139 on terrorism and added Chapter VI Bis on the financing of terrorism. In CTA6 it follows the 1970 addition of article 139 (T137).

what_happened: According to NACTA, Pakistan's 20-point National Action Plan for countering terrorism and extremism was approved on 24 December 2014 by a special session of Parliament.
summary: According to Pakistan's National Counter Terrorism Authority, the 20-point National Action Plan was approved by a special session of Parliament on 24 December 2014, after the 16 December 2014 attack on the Army Public School. NACTA states that it was later made the plan's monitoring body. The record comes from an undated NACTA page; the plan document itself is not in CTA6 [UNKNOWN].

what_happened: Pakistan's Anti-terrorism (Amendment) Act, 2020 (Act No. XX of 2020) received presidential assent and was published in the Gazette of Pakistan.
summary: On 30 July 2020 the Anti-terrorism (Amendment) Act, 2020 received the assent of Pakistan's President and was published the same day in the Gazette of Pakistan by the National Assembly Secretariat in Islamabad. It amends the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (T195), including provisions on legal persons and a new offence of failing to comply with orders under the United Nations (Security Council) Act, 1948.

what_happened: The National Human Rights Commission of Korea told the Speaker of the National Assembly that a pending amendment adding the purpose of obstructing the democratic organisation and activities of political parties to the Anti-Terrorism Act's definition of terrorism needs careful review.
summary: On 27 March 2026 the National Human Rights Commission of Korea gave the Speaker of the National Assembly its opinion on a pending amendment to the Act on Anti-Terrorism for the Protection of Citizens and Public Security, according to its press release of 1 April 2026. The Commission said the amendment raises concerns under the principles of clarity and proportionality (its assessment). It connects to the 2016 enforcement decree (T219) and the Commission's earlier opinions (T231, T232).
